n_ctx_note: Chat context granted for this run, read from the daemon log ('Creating chat LlamaContext (n_ctx=32768...)'). Well above the ~6600-token agent system prompt, so this run was not context-starved - the failure mode where every turn dies on 'Context window exceeded' and no-tool assertions score as passes.
note: Honest baseline: measured AFTER eval-prompt contamination was removed from agent guidance. Recorded on a purged database so every prompt/skill node was reseeded from the compiled constants - a reused DB keeps old seeded guidance and silently measures the pre-fix prompts. Not comparable to the earlier 11/12, which was measured with eval prompts planted in the guidance.
caveats: Scenario 3 is a FALSE PASS in this run. Its assertion (noExtraTypes) only checks that create_schema was called once; it does not check the schema persisted. Here create_schema returned is_error=true (title_template placeholders with no fields array) and no equipment type was registered. Scenario 4 then correctly reported the type did not exist and was scored a failure for it. Tracked in #1775.
Scenarios 4 and 6 are therefore downstream of scenario 3's silent failure, not independent defects. 8c (create_node retried after an error) is independent and real.

Control experiments run after this baseline, recorded here so the 8a/8b wording is not re-litigated from git archaeology: (a) trigger-vocabulary-free schema requests ('Set up somewhere to note down albums I mean to listen to', 'I want a place to jot down albums worth hearing') both fire create_schema correctly, so the DATABASE=SCHEMA rule generalizes and does not merely key on the words database/track/tracker/list; (b) scenario 4's wording is not the cause - an alternative instance phrasing behaves identically, because both are downstream of the missing schema.
